overall: The Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by cutting off an unnoticed public-comment topic at its June 21 meeting, but it did violate the Law by substituting an attachment for a summary in its June 7 minutes, and was ordered to amend them.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed a topic at its June 21 meeting that was not included on the posted meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: Where a public body does not actually engage in any deliberation on a particular topic, it cannot violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to the sufficiency of the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 7 minutes were insufficient because the Town Manager's Report was recorded only as 'See attached' with no summary of the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Simply attaching a report does not meet the Board’s obligation to summarize the discussion in its minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within thirty days of receipt of the letter, amend the June 7 minutes to include a summary of the discussion during the Town Manager's Report portion.
remedy_passage: We further order the Board, within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter, to amend the minutes of the June 7 meeting to include a summary of the discussion that took place during the Town Manager’s Report portion of the meeting.
